convoLines.text: "What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? You know?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together. …sorry."
"Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"It's like weather. You don't argue with weather. You build a roof."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on the big questions."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know where the chinese chive grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Since Megan died... I keep expecting to see Megan at the fire. Stupid."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
The future is a rumor. Today is a fact. I deal in facts.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Jesse shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
Done — their story has a crack in it now.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here? Allegedly."
"What's this about? The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said there was something you needed to say, to someone, and now you can't. Found another way to say it yet?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Mason. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Ivan owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I sleep with one ear uncovered, always. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said the most useful thing you learned is being hungry and going anyway. Still the lesson?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Ha." Not amused. "So you figured it out. Yeah, I took 1× Stone. What are you going to do about it?"
"Still on that personal stuff."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"They took Avery and Natalie — Hardened The Drop, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Hardened The Drop. They just... took Avery and Natalie. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"My part? I sleep with one ear uncovered, always and stay ready."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Actually, forget it."

deathBeat: d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Megan Sethi is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d12: 🕯️ Megan Sethi is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d13: That night, they bring Megan home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d12: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d12: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d12: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
burialWindowSay: d13: That night, they bring Megan home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d15: You say a few words for Megan. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d15: Burying the bloating dead was honest work, and it cost you. Fever by nightfall. (-10 health)
d15: You bury Megan. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
